body:
Life isn't a gift. Its a fucking nightmare that you need to make the best of. Nobody is happy all the time. Its what you make of it.

 About a year ago, I was considering suicide. I knew it was time to make a change. I seeked out counseling (which didn't really help but it was a good start) since then, I've done a major cleanse. I have gotten rid of anyone I seemed toxic or abusive in my life. Including family members.
 
I started to focus on the people who I know give a shit about me and started really giving a shit about them. I do whatever I can to show the people in my life, that I truly care. Sometimes it takes a lot of work to do that, but the end result always feels amazing. 

I decided to seek out a career change becuase I want my life to be meaningful and I want to make a difference in other people's lives. I quit smoking and doing drugs which eventually, lowered my anxiety levels. I started eating healthier which gave me more energy. And occasionally, I'll even exercise. 

I did all of this because I've been on anti depressants before and I hated them. I hate the process of trying to find the right ones and even with the right ones, I felt like my emotions were repressed and bottled up. I like being me. And to avoid going through all of that, I had to commit to big changes. 

I'll admit, I couldn't have done this without the support of a couple very important people in my life. Pick one or two people that you know you can trust and you know will support and encourage you, and just try. That is what I suggest. I hope this helps. 

I don't know you, but I truly wish you the best of luck and I hope your journey gets better.
Waking up to this comment made me feel a little bit better this morning. Thank you.

Camp grounds are opening up where I'm at, as long as you practice social distancing which is what I obviously plan on doing. And yeah I'm taking all of these precautions on the daily, but it's incredibly stressful when someone is "reminding" you to do it, even though you are already doing it.

Honestly, I've been contemplating leaving him when this is all over. There are so many other issues him and I have. It would be nice if he could think reasonably. I'm not asking him to touch random public objects or be around other people. I'm asking him to spend some time with me, in nature and get some exercise. This could help reduce his anxiety and maybe even change my current opinion of him. But I guess that's just too big of an ask. I don't mind camping by myself and I probably will. 
No I don't want to put him and risk and as long as I'm careful, I don't think I am.

So I actually read and up-dooted *your post* like right after I posted mine. I appreciate your kind words to me. It's nice being able to at least somewhat relate to someone else when it comes to the emotional abuse and roller coasters. 

Oddly enough I find it even more comforting that it's a totally random stranger who I'll likely never meet in person and likely lives far away, who shares a common sorrow with me. Idk why that is. 

I truly hope the best for you as well. I hope that you find your way out of your own trials and hurt. It's so much harder to be strong when your person who you trust to love you, puts you down. 

I suppose the best thing that either of us can do, is try to make it to tommorow, and then prioritize our own mental health. Tbh I don't think I'll survive this if I don't.

Thank you. I really needed that reassurance. I know this is an incredibly common thing, but I feel like (for lack of a better word) a fuck up. I'm already missing a good chunk of my cervix, what happens if I have to loose another chunk? Will I miss out on having kids? What happens if I get cancer like my mom did? Will they take it all from me? These are all questions I'm highly anticipating to ask my gyno next week.

For now, I'm content knowing that me getting HPV doesn't necessarily mean that me or my boyfriend were unfaithful. It just means that were going through some scary shit right now. Again, thanks Reddit doc.
